key_insight: Putting trainable nonlinear functions on the connections of physical neural networks, rather than using device nonlinearities only as weights, enables efficient continuous-value computation in low-power analogue hardware.
engineering_relevance: This approach is especially useful for smooth control and regression tasks in embedded systems, with a projected CMOS power draw of about 30 microwatts and a path to hardware-efficient analogue AI.
method: Inspired by Kolmogorov-Arnold networks, the model makes each physical connection a learnable nonlinear element.
Implemented these nonlinear functions as analogue band-pass filters on field-programmable analogue arrays.
Also tested transfer to hardware and a memristive simulation to verify the mechanism is device-agnostic.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong results on smooth targets such as robotic kinematics, continuous control, and photovoltaic maximum-power-point tracking, with quantified fidelity across roughly 35,000 connections.
watch_item: The advantage is task-dependent and does not extend well to classification-like decision boundaries, so it may not outperform MLPs on discrete classification problems.
paper_title: Low-power analogue neural networks with trainable nonlinear connections for continuous control
